TextBlock.Text: THEATRE The Sibutu Passage
DATE 29 October 2028 · 0320 local
SIDE Philippine Navy
WINDOW 120 min, closes at 180
HTMS Chakri Naruebet. Photo: PH3 ALEX C. WITTE, USN · Public domain · cropped
"Simply stated, strategic deterrence is about communicating capability and intent."
- Adm. Cecil D. Haney, Commander, US Strategic Command

SIBUTU PASSAGE, 0320. Signals and a fisherman in Sitangkai agree that a trawler under the Panama flag came out of Tarakan two days ago and is coming north up the passage tonight, low in the water. Two fast boats left Tawi-Tawi at midnight and are waiting for her west of Sibutu. What she carries was bought with the money that rides the semi-submersibles: rifles, mortars, parts for the drones on the Jolo ridge.

Two other Okean-class trawlers are fishing the passage tonight, both Philippine. A container ship is northbound for Sandakan's anchorage and a Malaysian tanker is going south. A helicopter has been flying from the Sabah side to a point in the passage and back since 0200 without a flight plan.

BRP Apolinario Mabini is east of the passage, BRP Florencio Inigo in it to the south, and Tawi 22 is up out of Sanga-Sanga. Weapons are Free on the trawler, the boats and the helicopter once each is classified. Fishermen in Sitangkai say she has a tube in her stern housing. Believe them.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.
Naval Forces Western Mindanao
COMMANDER'S INTENT

Stop the trawler before she reaches the boats waiting for her. She is one of three Okean-class trawlers in the passage and the other two are fishing. She is armed with something we have not seen; keep your distance until you know which she is, then do not give her the chance. The helicopter shuttling to her is Meridian's. The Malaysian side of the passage is theirs: stay in our water.
• Stop the armed trawler before she reaches the boats
• Classify the armed trawler
• Stop the fast boats
• Classify the shuttle helicopter
• Bring BRP Apolinario Mabini home
• Harm no fishing trawler or merchant ship

The Tawi-Tawi patrol group: BRP Apolinario Mabini, the patrol boat Florencio Inigo and the Navy helicopter Tawi 22 out of Sanga-Sanga. Opposing: one armed trawler under the Panama flag, two fast boats and a Bell 212 helicopter. Neutral: two fishing trawlers, a container ship and a tanker.

The planned window is 120 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 60 minutes more; the operation is closed at 180 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
